items.stem: During an interim valuation, a contractor claims payment for steel delivered to site but not yet installed. Under a typical standard contract, how is this usually treated?

options.text: It may be paid as materials on site, subject to the contract's conditions
options.rationale: Correct: unfixed materials properly on site are commonly payable if contract conditions are met.

options.text: It can never be included until the steel is fixed in place
options.rationale: Many contracts allow payment for materials on site before fixing.

options.text: It must be paid in full regardless of any conditions
options.rationale: Payment is subject to conditions such as protection and title.

options.text: It is treated as a variation
options.rationale: Delivery of planned materials is not a variation.

items.explanation: Correct: unfixed materials properly on site are commonly payable if contract conditions are met.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are core reasons for using a standard method of measurement? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It makes quantities comparable between different estimators and tenderers
options.rationale: Correct: common rules allow like-for-like comparison of bills.

options.text: It sets consistent rules for what to include, exclude and deduct
options.rationale: Correct: the method defines measurement conventions so takes-off are consistent.

options.text: It removes the need to read the drawings
options.rationale: Measurement still requires reading the drawings carefully.

options.text: It guarantees the project cannot exceed budget
options.rationale: Consistent measurement does not by itself control out-turn cost.

items.explanation: Correct: common rules allow like-for-like comparison of bills.

items.stem: A take-off measures a concrete slab at its full gross area and ignores a large opening the rules say must be deducted. What is the result?

options.text: The quantity of concrete is overstated
options.rationale: Correct: failing to deduct the opening inflates the measured volume and the priced cost.

options.text: The quantity is unaffected because openings are never deducted
options.rationale: The method's rules require the deduction; ignoring it is an error.
The unit rate is unaffected; the quantity is wrong.
A measurement error is not a variation.

items.explanation: Correct: failing to deduct the opening inflates the measured volume and the priced cost.
